title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the 2020 Committee report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its plans to develop clear guidelines and standards for AI use. It details key actions, partnerships with industry, and future steps to ensure AI systems are safe, transparent, and aligned with public values.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in England’s qualifications sector, setting out rules and guidance to keep assessments fair and reliable. The policy aims to protect students, maintain exam integrity, and ensure AI tools are transparent, secure, and support high-quality learning and assessment outcomes.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how AI systems rely on copyrighted works and explores the legal, economic, and societal impacts of this practice. It offers recommendations to balance protection for creators with the need for continued innovation in AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency” by outlining a comprehensive strategy to strengthen AI governance, boost innovation, and address ethical and workforce challenges. It emphasizes collaboration with industry and academia, updates regulatory frameworks, and commits to investing in research to keep the UK at the forefront of responsible AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document lays out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will review artificial intelligence in relation to public standards. It also includes FAQs that clarify the committee’s role, expectations, and key focus areas.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. In their submission, CSPL likely outlines recommendations and concerns related to AI regulation and oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how AI technologies influence the rules and approval processes for medical products and seeks to integrate the guidance from the AI White Paper into existing regulations. It aims to balance safety, transparency, and innovation by updating standards, testing protocols, and oversight mechanisms to accommodate AI-driven medical solutions.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: This strategy aims to make the defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI user in the world for its size. It focuses on leveraging AI to strengthen defence capabilities, improve operational efficiency, and build confidence among stakeholders.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to harness AI opportunities while carefully managing related risks. It outlines strategies, governance measures, and oversight mechanisms to ensure AI technologies are deployed safely and benefit society.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report looks at how copyrighted material is being used to train AI systems, checking that it follows the rules set out in Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It details progress made so far, highlights any problems, and suggests ways to keep AI development compliant and ethical.
